newsitem.title: USA: United Airlines explored exclusive aircraft deal.
newsitem.headline: United Airlines explored exclusive aircraft deal.

text.p: United Airlines said it has studied the benefits of an exclusive aircraft purchase contract but said it still sees advantages in having competition between manufacturers.

United, the nation's largest airline, said it has had discussion with Airbus Industrie and Boeing Co for potential replacement aircraft which would continue the "retire and replace" fleet program announced in 1995.
United is a unit of UAL Corp.

The recent exclusive supply contracts forged between Boeing and AMR Corp's American Airlines and Delta Air Lines Inc led "United to discuss the potential advantages of such an agreement," the airline said.

"We are currently satisfied with our contractual agreements with both Airbus and Boeing for new aircraft, however we are always searching for ways to improve them," said United Chairman Gerald Greenwald.
"Although we have discussed the potential advantages of such an exclusive agreement, we still see significant advantages in competition," Greenwald said in a prepared statement.
Over the next five years, United said it will take delivery of 16 Airbus 319s, 28 Airbus 320s, 24 Boeing 747-400s, six Boeing 757s and 16 Boeing 777s.
